title: Ivo, Father of Rav
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman describes him as one of the five sons of Abba bar Acha bar Sala of Kafri, citing [Sanhedrin 5a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.5a.12). In his account of [Rashi on Pesachim 4a](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Pesachim.4a.1.1), Ivo married “Ima,” R’ Chiyya’s sister, and R’ Chiyya is called his brother through their mother.

Hyman says that no halakhic ruling is mentioned in his name except in Sukkah 44a, with the corresponding reports at [44b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sukkah.44b.5-6): Ivo said, “I was standing before R’ Elazar bar R’ Tzadok,” and elsewhere on that page [transmits a ruling in his name](https://www.sefaria.org/Sukkah.44b.8). [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Sukkah.44b.5.1) explains that Ivo is Rav’s father. Hyman argues in the entry on Rav that this Ivo is Rav’s grandson and that it SHOULD READ R’ Elazar bar Yitzchak there, as in Dikdukei Soferim (דק״ס), note 9.[^4]

notes.text: The marriage and maternal-brother wording is Hyman’s account of Rashi’s view. Sanhedrin 5a names Ivo and Chiyya among sons of one Abba and discusses kinship, so the precise family configuration remains unresolved here. The later Ivo-as-grandson correction is Hyman’s separate claim.

No new primary scalar was returned. Hyman’s Rashi marriage account and precise maternal/sibling family configuration remain unresolved; the earlier Sanhedrin5a discussion names Ivo and Chiyya among one Abba’s sons but is not newly inspected. All five sons and full Abba>Acha>Sala chain remain. The no-other-halakhah statement is Hyman’s survey claim. Father-of-Rav is attributed to Rashi; the competing grandson identification and categorical SHOULD READ Elazar bar Yitzchak are Hyman’s separate arguments. Uninspected R-A and abbreviated titles are not promoted to full Rabbi. Dikdukei Soferim note9 stays a source report, not new collation.

Hyman’s printed article (vol. I, p. 138) cites Pesachim 4a, whereas the supplied text gives 60a. In the consulted Rashi on 4a, Ivo, Rav’s father, is R’ Chiyya’s brother on their father’s side, and Rav’s mother, “Ima,” is R’ Chiyya’s sister on their mother’s side. Sanhedrin 5a lists the five sons and reads Karsalla for the final name element where Hyman gives bar Sala. The Ivo reports are at Sukkah 44b in the consulted text. Rashi there calls the first Ivo Rav’s father, while the surrounding passage also names an Ivo among Rav’s daughter’s sons. Hyman argues for the grandson and cites a different reading for the teacher in Dikdukei Soferim, note 9. That apparatus has not been independently collated here.

The [Ivo entry in Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=385&lang=en) also cites Sukkah 44b and reports the Elazar bar Yitzchak variant from Yuchasin. It records a possible chronological reason for that reading, alongside witnesses with Elazar bar Tzadok.
